# Collaboration and geographic networks

::: {.learning-objectives}
**Learning objectives**

- Construct author and country collaboration networks.
- Distinguish affiliation geography from recruitment geography.
- Compare whole and fractional publication counting.
:::

## Collaboration relation

A collaboration network represents co-occurrence of authors, institutions, or countries on publications. It describes publication relationships, not the quality, equality, or intensity of the underlying collaboration.

```{r}
#| label: collaboration-load

source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R"))
M <- load_demo_data()

collaboration_fields <- c("AU", "C1", "AU_CO", "AU_UN")

M |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(collaboration_fields),
      ~ sum(!is.na(.x) & nzchar(trimws(as.character(.x))))
    )
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "field", values_to = "available") |>
  mutate(
    total = nrow(M),
    percent_available = round(100 * available / total, 1)
  )
```

For a real database export, extract countries and institutions from affiliations:

```r
M <- bibliometrix::metaTagExtraction(M, Field = "AU_CO", sep = ";")
M <- bibliometrix::metaTagExtraction(M, Field = "AU_UN", sep = ";")
```

## Country collaboration

```{r}
#| label: country-collaboration

country_matrix <- bibliometrix::biblioNetwork(
  M,
  analysis = "collaboration",
  network = "countries",
  sep = ";"
)

country_plot <- bibliometrix::networkPlot(
  country_matrix,
  normalize = "association",
  weighted = TRUE,
  n = min(30, nrow(country_matrix)),
  Title = "Country collaboration network",
  type = "fruchterman",
  size = 5,
  size.cex = TRUE,
  remove.multiple = FALSE,
  labelsize = 0.7,
  community.repulsion = 0,
  seed = 20261126
)

country_statistics <- bibliometrix::networkStat(country_matrix)
```

## Author collaboration

```{r}
#| label: author-collaboration

author_matrix <- bibliometrix::biblioNetwork(
  M,
  analysis = "collaboration",
  network = "authors",
  sep = ";"
)

author_plot <- bibliometrix::networkPlot(
  author_matrix,
  normalize = "association",
  weighted = TRUE,
  n = min(35, nrow(author_matrix)),
  Title = "Author collaboration network",
  type = "fruchterman",
  size = 5,
  size.cex = TRUE,
  remove.multiple = FALSE,
  labelsize = 0.7,
  community.repulsion = 0,
  seed = 20261126
)

author_statistics <- bibliometrix::networkStat(author_matrix)
```

Author-name disambiguation must be checked before interpreting centrality. Initials, name changes, transliteration, and database indexing errors can split or merge identities.

## Whole and fractional country counts

Under whole counting, every contributing country receives one publication. Under fractional counting, a paper with `k` countries contributes `1/k` to each.

```{r}
#| label: country-counting

country_counts <- M |>
  select(SR, AU_CO) |>
  separate_rows(AU_CO, sep = ";") |>
  mutate(AU_CO = str_squish(AU_CO)) |>
  group_by(SR) |>
  mutate(
    number_countries = n_distinct(AU_CO),
    fractional_weight = 1 / number_countries
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(country = AU_CO) |>
  summarise(
    whole_count = n_distinct(SR),
    fractional_count = sum(fractional_weight),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(whole_count))

country_counts
```

Use whole counting as an easily understood primary summary and fractional counting as a sensitivity analysis, or reverse the order if contribution allocation is central to the research question.

## Affiliation is not recruitment

The country in an author's affiliation must not be interpreted as the country where participants were recruited. Use a separately extracted `RECRUITMENT_COUNTRY` variable from full reports or trial registries.

```{r}
#| label: recruitment-geography

M |>
  separate_rows(RECRUITMENT_COUNTRY, sep = ";") |>
  count(RECRUITMENT_COUNTRY, sort = TRUE)
```

## Exercise

Identify a country whose whole-count rank differs materially from its fractional-count rank. Explain the collaboration pattern that produces the difference.
